text_blocks.snippet: The Families First Coronavirus Response Act (FFCRA) was a U.S. federal law enacted on March 11, 2020, in response to the COVID-19 pandemic.
The FFCRA aimed to provide financial assistance and support to individuals and families impacted by the pandemic, particularly those who were unable to work due to COVID-19.

list.title: Paid sick leave:
list.snippet: Provided up to 14 days of paid sick leave to employees who were diagnosed with COVID-19, quarantined, or caring for a family member with COVID-19.

list.title: Emergency family and medical leave:
list.snippet: Extended the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) to provide up to 12 weeks of paid leave for employees who were unable to work due to COVID-19-related reasons, including caring for a child whose school or childcare was closed.

list.title: Unemployment benefits:
list.snippet: Expanded unemployment benefits to individuals who were laid off or furloughed due to COVID-19.

list.title: Food assistance:
list.snippet: Increased funding for food assistance programs, such as Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP).

list.title: Testing and contact tracing:
list.snippet: Provided funding for COVID-19 testing, contact tracing, and public health infrastructure.

text_blocks.snippet: Most provisions of the FFCRA expired on December 31, 2021. However, some provisions related to unemployment benefits were extended through September 30, 2022.

The FFCRA played a significant role in mitigating the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic by providing financial support to millions of Americans who were unable to work. It also helped to expand access to healthcare and public health services.
